sentence: This project studies how a receptor for opioids changes signaling from the dorsal striatum to the substantia nigra after acute and chronic opioid treatment.
This project tries to find out why some people are more adversely affected by ozone exposure than others.
This project builds a portal that shares brain images and genetic data from stroke patients so investigators can study them.
This project uses long-read sequencing to look at differences in the DNA and RNA of patients with dementias that are not Alzheimer’s disease.
This project offers tissue clearing and imaging methods to map brain circuits involved in drug addiction.
This project studies how the different enzymatic activities of epigenetic modifiers regulate neural stem cells.
This project tries to find out how mutations in a nuclear envelope protein disrupt chromatin organization and gene regulation during muscle cell differentiation.
This project studies how an amino acid change keeps smooth muscle alpha-actin out of the nucleus and leaves smooth muscle cells incompletely differentiated.
This project builds a gene editing therapy for cystic fibrosis using targeted exon replacement.
This project offers genetic and genomic assays, including sequencing and single-cell profiling, to support cancer researchers.
This project studies how a gene mutation reduces the expression of a synthetase in cells and in a mouse model of hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
This project uses clonal analysis in the zebrafish testis to study male fertility across the lifespan and disorders linked to advanced paternal age.
This project records brain activity and pupil size in naturally sleeping mice to study how memories are added without disturbing existing knowledge.
This project offers sequencing services that measure gene expression, chromosome structure and nucleotide sequence for researchers.
This project studies how pericytes, cells that envelop brain blood vessels, contribute to early blood flow deficits in a mouse model of disease.
This project studies how metabolic dysregulations govern tumor development, metastasis, drug resistance and recurrence.
This project develops oligonucleotide drugs that selectively block a target active in glioblastoma tumor growth and invasion.
This project uses large language models to harmonize clinical vocabularies and specify computable phenotypes from real-world data.
This project builds open-source machine-learning models that predict thrombosis and bleeding in patients with cancer.
This project tries to prevent rejection of cardiac xenografts by producing immune hyporesponsiveness at transplantation so a less lethal immunosuppressive regimen can follow.
